items.where: agi, then /voice typed in the composer of an open chat
steps: Run agi in the terminal and open an existing chat from the chat list.
Type /voice in the composer and press Enter.

items.needs: a microphone and a build with voice support
items.note: There is no separate voice button. /voice runs in whichever session is open (app.session), so it is bound to that chat by design.

items.needs: a microphone and a build with voice support

items.where: agi, then /voice in an open chat, then ESC; the spoken turns appear in the chat after voice ends

items.note: During voice the terminal shows only the voice prompts. The chat view (where spoken turns are merged) is shown again only after voice ends, so the transcript is not live inside the chat view.

items.where: /voice, then press SPACE to start recording

items.where: /voice, then SPACE to record, then ENTER to stop and ENTER to send
steps: Type /voice and press Enter in an open chat.
Press SPACE, say a short sentence, then press ENTER to stop.
Read the transcript line "You said:" and press ENTER to send.
Watch for the spinner text "Thinking..." while the reply is produced, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a microphone and a build with voice support
items.note: The spinner also shows "Transcribing..." before the reply. No indicator specific to tool runs was found in voice.rs.

items.where: /voice, then SPACE to record; the level bar appears next to REC
steps: Type /voice and press Enter in an open chat.
Press SPACE and speak; watch the bar in brackets next to "REC".
Stop with ENTER and compare the bar with Expected: it should move with your voice level.
items.needs: a microphone and a build with voice support
items.note: The bar is a text meter of microphone level during recording only. No visual that follows reply audio was found in voice.rs.

items.where: /voice, then ESC at the "[SPACE to record, ESC to exit]" prompt
steps: Type /voice and press Enter in an open chat.
Press ESC at the prompt "[SPACE to record, ESC to exit]".

items.where: /voice, then hold SPACE to record and release it to stop

Hold SPACE, speak, and release SPACE.

Press ENTER to send the transcript.
items.needs: a microphone and a build with voice support

labels.text: (release SPACE or press ENTER to stop)

items.note: Release is detected only when the terminal reports key releases. Otherwise ENTER is the stop key. After stopping, the text waits for ENTER before it is sent, so it does not send on release by itself.

items.where: /voice es (or /voice fr, etc.) in the composer, or agi --voice-lang es at launch

items.note: The supported codes are in apps/cli/src/voice_languages.rs. Language is fixed per voice session; to change it, exit and type /voice with a new code. Whether recognition uses it was not traced beyond the transcribe call.

items.needs: a microphone and a build with voice support

Check that the reply continues the same chat with the earlier spoken turns, compare with Expected.

items.needs: a microphone and a build with voice support

items.where: Type /agents (no words after it) in the AGI CLI chat screen. It opens the "Agents" list.
steps: Start the app with agi, then type /agents and press Enter.
Look for the "Agents" box: each row shows the name, color, scope (project or global), model and description.
Type part of a name in the search line to filter the list, then press Esc to close it.
To remove one, type /agents delete <name> --yes (without --yes it only shows a warning that the delete cannot be undone).
To change one, type /agents set <name> <field> <value>, then /agents show <name> to see the result.
Compare with Expected: open, edit and remove are all reachable, but the list itself has no edit or remove buttons, and Enter activates the agent instead of opening an editor.
items.needs: at least one custom assistant already created
items.note: The list is a picker: Enter activates an agent. Edit and remove are typed commands, not buttons in the list.

items.where: Type /agents create <description> (several words, for an AI-drafted assistant) or /agents create <name> (one word, for a blank template) in the chat screen.
steps: Type /agents create (with nothing after it) and press Enter to see the "Create new agent" help.
Type /agents create reviews pull requests for risky changes and press Enter.
Wait for "Generating agent configuration..." to finish.
Type /agents and press Enter to check that the new agent appears in the "Agents" list.
For a blank template, type /agents create my-reviewer and press Enter, then check for "Created project agent `my-reviewer` at" in the reply.
Compare with Expected: the new assistant can be created from the product, and it shows up in the list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a model for the description form; none for the blank template
items.note: The description form runs a model request. A single word creates a blank template instead.

items.where: Type /agents set <name> <field> <value> in the chat screen. There is no form or editor screen; each command changes one field.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer description Reviews risky pull requests and press Enter, using the name of an assistant you made.
Read the reply: it should say the field was updated.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the new description shows in the details.
Repeat with another field, for example /agents set reviewer model <model name> or /agents set reviewer tools read_file, search_files.
Note the editable fields listed in the "Fields:" line: description, model, color, tools, disallowedTools, skills, maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd, permissionMode, prompt.
items.needs: a custom assistant to change
items.note: Expected asks for a form or editor; the product offers one typed command per field instead.

items.where: Type /agents rename <name> <new-name> in the chat screen, then type /agents to check the list.
steps: Type /agents rename reviewer code-reviewer and press Enter.
Read the reply: it should say the agent was renamed.
Type /agents and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the new name is shown in the "name" column of the "Agents" list.
Type /agents show code-reviewer and check the "Agent:" heading.
items.needs: a custom assistant to rename
items.note: The new name is turned into a lowercase slug, so spaces and capitals are removed in the saved name.

items.where: Type /agents set <name> description <text> in the chat screen, then type /agents to see it in the list.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer description Reviews risky pull requests and press Enter.
Type /agents and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the description appears in the list row for reviewer.
Clear it with /agents set reviewer description and check that the row shows "(no description)".
items.needs: a custom assistant to describe

items.where: Type /agents set <name> prompt <text> in the chat screen, then /agents show <name> to read it back.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer prompt You review code for security problems only and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Check the "Prompt:" section at the bottom of the reply for the new text.
Type /agents reviewer to activate it. The reply should say Agent `reviewer` activated.
Ask a question in the chat and compare the answer with the instructions in Expected.
items.needs: a custom assistant to give instructions to

items.where: Type /agents set <name> model <model name> in the chat screen, then /agents show <name>. Model names come from the model list in the product.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer model <model name> and press Enter, using a model name the product accepts.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Check the "model:" line in the reply for the chosen model.
Type /agents reviewer to activate it.
Compare with Expected: the reply should say Agent `reviewer` activated and show "(model: ...)" with the pinned model.
items.needs: a model name that this account can use
items.note: If the model cannot be switched, the product prints "model override ignored" instead.

items.where: Type /agents set <name> tools <tool names> in the chat screen, or /agents set <name> disallowedTools <tool names> to block some. Check the result with /agents show <name>.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer tools read_file, search_files and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Check the "tools:" line in the reply.
Type /agents set reviewer disallowedTools web_fetch to block one tool, then /agents show reviewer again.
Compare with Expected: the tools line lists only the chosen tools, and the disallowed one appears under "disallowed_tools".
items.needs: a custom assistant to change
items.note: The product has no list of tool names to pick from; the names are typed by hand. The name web_fetch appears in the source, and the picker shows tools: all when no list is set.

The only per-assistant control is the tools and disallowedTools list, which takes tool names; I did not find a product-defined web-search tool name outside tests. Searched the CLI source for web_search, web search and per-agent options.

No connector picker was found. The only way found is editing the file that /agents path <name> prints. Searched for connector, mcp and mcpServers in the CLI source.

items.needs: none
items.note: No private setting for an assistant was found. Assistants are markdown files: project scope in .agiworkforce/agents and global scope in the user folder, shown as scope in the list. Searched apps/cli/src/agents.rs for private, visibility and share.

items.needs: none

Look for a read_file tool line that shows the path.
Check that the answer matches the file's contents.
items.needs: a text file in the folder

items.where: agi, then ask in chat to create a file
steps: Start agi in a folder that agi may write to.
Type a request to create a file named notes.txt with one line of text, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for a write_file tool line that shows the path, then check that notes.txt exists in the folder.
items.needs: a folder agi may write to

items.where: agi, then ask in chat to write and run a short Python script
steps: Start agi.
Type a request to write a short Python script that prints 2 plus 2 and to run it, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for a line starting with $ and the printed result, and an exit line.
items.needs: Python installed on the machine
items.note: No separate code-execution tool was found; the script runs through the shell tool (run_command).

items.where: agi, then ask in chat to run a shell command
steps: Start agi in a folder with some files.
Type a request to run the command ls -la in this folder, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for a line starting with $ ls -la, the listing, and an exit 0 line.
items.needs: a Mac or Linux shell with ls

items.where: agi, then ask in chat to change one line of an existing file
steps: Create a text file with three lines in the folder.
Type a request to change the second line of that file to say hello, then press Enter.
If the Tool Approval box appears, choose Yes.
Look for the edit tool line and the changed line, and check the other lines are unchanged.
items.needs: a text file with three lines
items.note: The tool name edit_file appears in the catalog; I did not confirm how the diff is drawn beyond the edit result code.

items.where: agi, then type /chrome, then ask in chat to open a web page in the browser
steps: Start agi.
Type /chrome and press Enter.
Look for the Chrome integration text and a Paired line.
Type a request to open https://example.com in the browser, then press Enter.
Look for an Open line in the transcript that shows the address.
items.needs: AGI Desktop with its Chrome extension paired
items.note: Pairing state is shown by /chrome; I did not check the pairing steps themselves.

items.where: agi, then type /chrome, then ask in chat to read the page open in the browser
steps: Start agi with the browser paired (see /chrome).
Type a request to read the text of the page open in the browser, then press Enter.
Look for a transcript line that says Read the active tab.
Compare the answer with the text on the page.
items.needs: AGI Desktop with its Chrome extension paired and a page open
items.note: Clicking and typing use the same route with other browser tool names; the read line is the one given here.

items.where: agi, then type /image followed by a short description
steps: Start agi.
Type /image a red bicycle on a beach, then press Enter.
Wait for the generation to finish; a chip appears.
Type /image open to view the image.
Compare the image with the prompt.
items.needs: an account that can generate images
items.note: I did not confirm whether the image also appears inline in the transcript.

items.where: agi, then type /memory
steps: Start agi.
Type /memory and press Enter to see saved facts.
Type /memory add local and a short test fact, then press Enter.
Type /memory again and check that the new fact is listed.
items.needs: none
items.note: The assistant's memory tool is called by the model during a turn; this path covers the user's view of the same memory.

items.where: agi, then type /connectors
steps: Start agi on a managed account.
Type /connectors and press Enter.
Check that the text says connectors are offered to this session's turns.
Ask in chat about today's calendar events, then check for a tool line and an approval box before it runs.
items.needs: a managed account with Google Calendar connected on the connectors page
items.note: No dedicated calendar tool was found in the CLI; calendar access comes through a connector.

items.where: agi, then type /connectors
steps: Start agi on a managed account.
Type /connectors and press Enter.
Check that the text lists the connectors offered to this session.
Ask in chat to read the latest Slack message, then check for a tool line and an approval box before it runs.
items.needs: a managed account with Slack connected on the connectors page
items.note: No dedicated messaging tool was found in the CLI; Slack access comes through a connector.

items.where: agi, then type /schedule followed by what to run and when
steps: Start agi on an account that can use cloud schedules.
Type /schedule every day at 9am summarize today's notes, then press Enter.
Approve the schedule creation if asked.
Look for a cron_create tool line and confirm the new schedule is listed when you ask for your schedules.
items.needs: a managed account that can use cloud schedules
items.note: The delete and list actions use cron_delete and cron_list; I did not walk through them.

items.where: agi, then type /agents
steps: Start agi.
Type /agents and press Enter; an agent picker opens.
Pick an agent, or press Esc to close the picker.
Ask in chat to use a named agent, then look for an agent tool line that shows its name.
items.needs: at least one agent file, made with /agents create

items.where: agi, then ask in chat for a question with choices
steps: Start agi in an interactive terminal.
Type a request asking the assistant to ask you which of two options you want, then press Enter.
Look for a question box that shows the choices.
Pick one and check that the assistant continues with that choice.
items.needs: an interactive terminal
items.note: The plan marked this unverified; the ask_user tool and its question box were found in the code.

items.where: agi, then ask in chat for approval of a plan
steps: Start agi.
Type a request asking the assistant to get my approval of a plan before doing anything, then press Enter.
Look for the Tool Approval box with a question.
Choose Yes and check that the assistant continues; choose No and check that it stops.
items.needs: none

items.where: not visible in the app; the list of tools the model can call appears under /tools
steps: Start agi.
Type /tools and press Enter.
Check the line that says Tools the model can call in this session with a count.
Ask a request that needs a tool not on that list and look for a tool_search line in the transcript.
items.needs: none
items.note: The note to the model about on-demand tools is in the system prompt and is not shown to the user.

items.where: agi, then ask in chat for a tool by topic
steps: Start agi.
Type a request that asks the assistant to find tools about files, then press Enter.
Look for a tool_search tool line in the transcript.
Check that the result lists matching tool names with descriptions.
items.needs: none
items.note: Keyword search is run by the model; the user has no search box. /tools lists all tools and /tools <name> needs an exact name.

items.where: agi, then type /tools, then /tools <name>
steps: Start agi.
Type /tools and press Enter to see the list of tools with descriptions.
Type /tools read_file and press Enter.
Check that the name, description, and a Parameters: section with the schema appear.
items.needs: none

items.where: agi, then ask in chat to run a command or change a file
steps: Start agi.
Type a request to run the command echo hello, then press Enter.
Look at the tool line; it should show the command after a $ sign.
If the Tool Approval box appears, check it shows the command before you choose Yes or No.
items.needs: none

items.where: agi, then ask in chat for any request that runs a tool
steps: Start agi.
Type a request to run the command sleep 5, then press Enter.
While it runs, look for a spinner on the tool line and the elapsed time in brackets.
When it finishes, look for a check mark for completed or a cross for failed, and the counts with working and completed.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code shows the counts text; I did not confirm exactly where on screen it is drawn.

items.where: agi, then ask in chat for any request that runs a tool
steps: Start agi in a folder with a few files.
Type a request to list the files in this folder, then press Enter.
Look for a short preview line under the tool line.
Check that the preview shows the first non-empty line of the result, shortened if long.
items.needs: none
items.note: The full output is shown with Ctrl-O, which is outside this item.

items.where: agi (chat screen), then press Ctrl-O; the key list in "/help" shows "Show or hide full tool output"
steps: Run agi and start a chat that makes a tool call (for example a shell command with several lines of output).
Find the finished tool call in the transcript and note its short result preview.
Press Ctrl-O. The status line shows "showing full tool output, Ctrl-O to collapse" and the output lines appear, up to 200, then "… N more lines" if longer.
Press Ctrl-O again. The status line shows "tool output collapsed" and the preview returns. Compare with Expected: the call expands and collapses.
items.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model that can call a shell tool

labels.text: Show or hide full tool output
showing full tool output, Ctrl-O to collapse

items.note: Ctrl-O toggles every tool output in the transcript at once, not one call. The expanded view shows the result only, not the arguments; arguments are shown through "/tools log <n>" (S57.37), so Expected's "full arguments" is not met by Ctrl-O alone.

items.where: agi (chat screen), then type /tools retry; the list shown by "/tools" says "/tools retry reruns the last failed call"
steps: Run agi and ask the assistant for a tool call that fails (for example reading a file that does not exist).
Look for the failed call in the transcript; its state shows as a red failed mark with the error.
Type /tools retry and press Enter. The assistant is sent a prompt to run the failed call again and report the result.
If no call failed, look for the message "No failed tool call in this session to retry." Compare with Expected: the error is shown, and the retry runs.
items.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model; a way to make a tool call fail

labels.text: /tools retry reruns the last failed call
No failed tool call in this session to retry.

items.note: The code shows the user-side retry (/tools retry). The failed-state mark is in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs ("✗" for TranscriptCellState::Failed). I did not confirm from the code that the error text is sent back to the model on its own, only that the retry prompt is built from the failed call; Expected's 'error goes back to the model' is therefore unverified.

items.where: agi (chat screen): a long tool result shows a notice at its end that begins "[full output saved for the user to" and gives a file path under the config folder's tool-output directory
steps: Run agi and ask the assistant to run a shell command that prints a very large amount of text (thousands of lines).
Look at the end of that tool result in the transcript for the notice that begins "[full output saved for the user to".
Open the path shown in the notice (in Finder or Terminal) and check that the full output is there.

Try asking the assistant to read that path with its file-read tool. Compare with Expected: the full text is stored and a reference is given; the code says the file-read tool cannot open it, so the reference is for the user only.
items.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model that can run a shell command; a command with large output

labels.text: [full output saved for the user to

items.note: The code stores the output in the config folder's tool-output directory and tells the model that read_file cannot open it. The Expected line says the model can open it later, which the code contradicts; the tester should check that point against the notice text. The exact path is built at run time, so no fixed path is given.

items.where: agi (chat screen), then type /tools log; then /tools log <n> for one call in full
steps: Run agi and make two or three tool calls in the chat (for example a shell command and a file read).
Type /tools log and press Enter. A numbered list shows each call with its name, input and outcome.
Type /tools log 1 (or another number) and press Enter. It shows the call's name, its input as JSON, and its result, marked "(failed)" if it failed.
Compare with Expected: each call's tool, input and outcome can be reviewed afterwards.
items.needs: a Free account or paid account with a model; the calls must be made in the same session

labels.text: /tools log <n> shows one call in full.

items.note: The log reads the tool calls of the current session (session_tool_runs). The code does not show it kept after the session ends, so a tester should check whether a resumed session still lists older calls.

items.where: Type "agi mcp list" in a terminal, or type "/mcp" in the agi chat screen
steps: Run: agi mcp list
Look for one row per registered server, each with its name, a status word (enabled, disabled or blocked), its transport and its target.
If no servers exist, look for the line that names the registry file.
Compare with Expected: a list of configured MCP servers.
items.needs: none
items.note: The list comes from the local registry file (~/.agiworkforce/mcp.json) and project MCP files; the code shows no account or workspace-level server list.

items.where: Type "agi mcp add <name> --command <executable>" in a terminal (in chat, "/mcp add <name> stdio <command>")
steps: Run: agi mcp add my-local-server --command node --arg server.js (use any executable on this Mac)
Read the confirmation line that starts with "Registered MCP server".
Run: agi mcp list and check the new row appears with status enabled.
Run: agi mcp get my-local-server and check the transport shows stdio and the target shows the command.
items.needs: a local executable for a stdio server
items.note: The product starts a stdio server only when a session starts or /mcp restart runs; the add command itself does not launch it.

items.where: Type "agi mcp add <name> --url <url>" in a terminal (in chat, "/mcp add <name> <url>")
steps: Run: agi mcp add my-remote --url https://example.com/mcp (use a real remote MCP URL)
Read the line that starts with "Registered MCP server".
Optional credentials: add --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>" to the same command, then check with agi mcp get my-remote.
Run: agi mcp list and check the row shows the URL with status enabled.
items.needs: a remote MCP server URL; a token if the server needs one

labels.text: Header for a remote server as "Name: value", for example an API key. Repeat for each.

items.note: none

items.where: Type "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal to view, then "agi mcp add <name> --url <url> --force" to edit
steps: Run: agi mcp get my-remote and read the name, status, transport, target and file lines.
Run: agi mcp add my-remote --url https://new.example.com/mcp --force to replace the entry.
Run: agi mcp get my-remote again and check the target now shows the new URL.
Compare with Expected: the URL, transport and arguments can be viewed and changed.
items.needs: an existing registered server

labels.text: Replace an existing entry with the same name.

items.note: There is no interactive editor screen; editing is done by re-running add with --force (or /mcp reconfigure in chat).

items.where: Type "agi mcp add <name> --command <executable> --env KEY=VALUE" in a terminal
steps: Run: agi mcp add my-local-server --command node --arg server.js --env API_REGION=us-east-1
Read the line that starts with "Registered MCP server".
Run: agi mcp get my-local-server and check the file line points to the registry where the entry is stored.
Compare with Expected: the variable is set for the stdio server.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Environment variable for a stdio server as KEY=VALUE, repeat for each.

items.note: The --env flag applies only to stdio servers (it requires --command). Env values are not shown by agi mcp get in the code read; no in-chat env command was found.

items.where: Type "agi mcp login <name>" in a terminal (for OAuth), or pass --header when adding a remote server
steps: Run: agi mcp login my-remote (for a remote server that offers OAuth)
Complete the sign-in in the browser that opens.
Read the line that starts with "Authorized MCP server" and check it says the token is stored in the OS credential store.
Optional: run agi mcp logout my-remote and read the sign-out result line.
items.needs: an outside account (the remote server's sign-in) and a remote server that offers OAuth

labels.text: Authorize a remote MCP server over OAuth and store the token.
The token is stored in the OS credential store.

items.note: Token-based credentials are entered with --header at add time; the stored OAuth token location is the OS credential store per the confirmation text.

items.where: Type "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal, or "/mcp restart" in the agi chat screen
steps: Make sure the server is enabled (agi mcp list shows enabled).
Run: agi mcp get my-remote and wait up to 20 seconds.
Read the connection line: it shows a connect error or "did not answer within 20 seconds" on failure, and the tool list on success.
Compare with Expected: the result shows whether the connection succeeded.
items.needs: a registered server (a remote one needs a reachable URL)
items.note: A disabled server shows only the turn-on hint and no connection test. /mcp test runs the same reconnect as /mcp restart.

items.where: Type "/mcp tools" in the agi chat screen, or "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal
steps: Connect a server first (agi mcp get <name> or /mcp restart).
In chat, type: /mcp tools
Read the heading "MCP tools:" and check each tool row lists its server name and description.
Optional: type /mcp tools <server-name> and check only that server's tools appear.
items.needs: a connected MCP server that offers tools
items.note: none

items.where: Type "/" in the agi chat screen and find the entries that start with "[MCP:", or type "/mcp:<server>:<prompt>"
steps: Connect a server that offers prompts (/mcp restart).
Type / in the chat input and look for commands whose description starts with [MCP:<server-name>].
Choose one and run it, then read the reply in chat.
Compare with Expected: the prompt is listed and runs.
items.needs: a connected MCP server that offers prompts

labels.text: Run a connected server's prompt as /mcp:<server>:<prompt>

items.note: Prompt commands are registered only when the server offers prompts; the [MCP: prefix text is built in tui_app.rs.

items.where: Type "/mcp info <server>" in the agi chat screen, or "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal
steps: Connect the server first (/mcp restart).
In chat, type: /mcp info <server-name>
Read the Protocol line, the server name and version, and the Capabilities line.
Compare with Expected: protocol, tools, resources, prompts and extensions are visible.
items.needs: a connected MCP server
items.note: The Capabilities line lists the advertised capability names; resources, prompts and extensions are not shown as separate sections in the code read.

items.where: Type "/mcp info <server>" for health, or "/mcp logs <server>" for recent logs, in the agi chat screen
steps: Connect the server first (/mcp restart).
In chat, type: /mcp info <server-name> and read whether it says responding or not responding.
Type: /mcp logs <server-name> and read the Recent output section.
Compare with Expected: health and recent logs are visible; no call history was found in the code.
items.needs: a connected MCP server

labels.text: No output from this server yet.

items.note: No call history view was found; only status and recent output lines are shown.

items.where: Type "agi mcp disable <name>" and "agi mcp enable <name>" in a terminal, or "/mcp disable <name>" and "/mcp enable <name>" in chat
steps: Run: agi mcp disable my-remote and read the Disabled MCP server line.
Run: agi mcp list and check the status is disabled and the row is still there.
Run: agi mcp enable my-remote and check the status returns to enabled.
Compare with Expected: the server is kept while off and can be turned back on.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Turn a registered MCP server off without removing it.

items.note: A running session keeps a disabled server until /mcp restart.

items.where: Put a .mcp.json file in the project folder, then type "/mcp" in agi started from that folder
steps: In a project folder, create a .mcp.json file with one server entry (or run agi init, which creates mcp.json).
Start agi from that folder in a terminal and approve the project servers when asked (the code says Run /trust grant in agi).
Type /mcp in the chat screen and check the server appears under the project scope.
Start agi from a different folder and check the server does not appear.
items.needs: a project folder you can write to; a terminal for the first approval
items.note: The approval step and the project-only scope are from code read; the exact on-screen review prompt was not confirmed.

items.needs: a server on a private network
items.note: Searched apps/cli/src/mcp for private network, relay, tunnel and bridge wording; only a URL check (apps/cli/src/mcp/registry.rs validate_remote_url) and unrelated sandbox text were found, and no private-network connector route was found.

items.needs: an in-development server on localhost
items.note: No developer-mode flow found; searched for developer mode, dev mode and localhost. The nearest path is agi mcp add <name> --url http://localhost:<port>, which validate_remote_url in apps/cli/src/mcp/registry.rs accepts, but that is not a dedicated developer-mode flow.

items.where: agi, then ask the agent to create a file; the approval prompt (Tool Approval) appears in the chat
steps: Start agi in an empty test folder.
Type: create a file named notes.txt with one line of text.
At the approval prompt press y (Yes).
Check the file is created and the agent carries on with its reply. Try again and press n instead: the file is not created and the agent carries on.

items.where: agi, then ask for several file changes in one request; the approval prompt has Allow All and Deny All
steps: Type: create three files named a.txt, b.txt and c.txt, each with one line.
At the first approval prompt press t (Allow All), or press d (Deny All) on a second try.
Check the remaining file requests in that turn are approved, or refused, without more prompts.

items.where: agi, then at an approval prompt press s (Allow Session)
steps: Type: create a file named s1.txt with one line.
At the approval prompt press s (Allow Session).
Type: create a file named s2.txt with one line.
Check no prompt appears for the second file this session. Restart agi and check it asks again.
items.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder

items.needs: none

items.where: agi, then type /add-dir <folder> and /remove-dir <folder> in the chat
steps: Type /add-dir alone to list the folders the agent may change.
Type /add-dir <path of a test folder> and read the reply.
Ask the agent to create a file in that folder and check it does.
Type /remove-dir <same path>, then ask again and check the agent no longer changes that folder.

steps: Type /permissions deny domain:example.com and read the reply.
Ask the agent to fetch https://example.com.
Check the fetch is refused and no page content comes back.

items.where: agi, then type /permissions allow <command prefix> in the chat; check later with agi approvals list in a terminal
steps: In the chat type /permissions allow ls.
Quit agi, then in a terminal run agi approvals list.
Start agi again and type /permissions; check the rule is still listed under Allow.
Check the rule shows in the list from agi approvals list.

steps: Run agi doctor --export in the folder where you want the file.
Read the printed summary above the Wrote line.

Compare with Expected: the release notes are shown from inside the product.
items.needs: an older CLI build than the latest release, so a newer release is available
items.note: The What's new notice is shown once per version, and only when the release has notes.

Find any model marked with ! and read its line deprecated, leaves the catalog <date> if one shows.

Type agi models list --json and look for supports_tools, supports_vision and supports_reasoning on each model.
Compare with Expected: the models your key can call, with capabilities and context size.

labels.text: List catalog models and discovered local models.
No models available to this CLI account tier.

Type /budget alone and check that it shows the cap.

items.where: Terminal > agi plugin install <folder> --integrity sha256:<hex> (get the hash from agi plugin digest <folder>)
steps: Pick an unpublished plugin folder on disk.
Type agi plugin digest <folder> and copy the sha256:<hex> value it prints.
Type agi plugin install <folder> --integrity sha256:<hex> and press Return.
Type agi plugin list and look for the plugin name in the installed list.
Compare with Expected: the unpublished plugin loads into your own account so you can try it.
items.needs: a plugin folder on disk
items.note: Whether a plain local folder is accepted as the install source is not confirmed (apps/cli/src/installs.rs:93 handles git sources; the local-path branch was not read), and the agi plugin digest command comes from a doc comment, not a read of its subcommand entry.

items.needs: external-service
items.note: The plan's Code line has no location. I searched apps/cli for attribution, lineage, provenance, 'copied from', 'copied_from' and publisher. The only hits were license text in apps/cli/assets/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt and Rust test code, so no product screen shows publisher, author, source or version lineage.

items.where: Terminal: type `agi marketplace add <owner/repo>` (also in chat: `/marketplace add <owner/repo>`). To view: `agi marketplace sources`, or in chat `/plugin`, then switch to the Marketplaces tab with the right arrow key.
steps: Sign in to the AGI CLI with an account that has the marketplace capability (canUseMarketplace). Without it the add step is refused.
In a terminal, type `agi marketplace add owner/repo` for a public GitHub repository that has a marketplace manifest. Optionally add `--ref <branch or tag>` and `--name <name>`.
Look for the line 'Added <name> to your account (<N> plugins).'
Type `agi marketplace sources`. Look for the new row with its id, its name, its status, its plugin count and its repository URL under 'Marketplaces on your account'.
In the chat, type `/plugin`, press the right arrow key until the Marketplaces tab shows, and look for the hint 'agi marketplace add <github url>'.
Compare with Expected: the publisher's marketplace is named (name and repository URL) and its plugins become available.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account with the marketplace capability, a public GitHub repository with a marketplace manifest
items.note: The Code line's apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3635 is unrelated: it is the 'Recent project folders' code. The real path is add_marketplace at apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2758 (clap 'marketplace add' at apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2340-2352) and the slash path at apps/cli/src/repl/mod.rs:353. The sources list shows a name and repository URL, but no separate publisher field; the 'Added' line shows only the source name.

items.where: Terminal: type "agi models status" (the same check runs with "agi models scan"; add --json for JSON output)
steps: Open a terminal and type: agi models status, then press Return.
Read the first line of output, which should be "Local model servers".
Look at each provider line: it shows the provider name, "running" or "not running", and the base URL.
If a provider shows "not running", check for the indented "error:" line under it and the models list ("models: none discovered" when nothing is found).
Start a local model server (such as Ollama), run agi models status again, and confirm the line changes to "running" and lists its models.
items.needs: a terminal with the AGI CLI installed; optional: a local model server such as Ollama to see a running state
items.note: The Expected line says the app shows health; here it is a CLI command output, and the TUI /models screen only points to agi models status and does not show health; agi doctor does not check the local runtime.

items.where: /voice typed at the agi prompt
steps: Type /voice and press Enter.
Press SPACE to start recording, say the request, then stop recording as the prompt shows.
Press ENTER to send the transcribed text (or e to edit it first).
Look at the chat: the request should be sent to the agent. Compare with Expected: it should become a background task that shows in Tasks.
items.needs: a microphone

labels.text: [ENTER to send, 'e' to edit, 'r' to re-record, ESC to discard]

items.note: The voice loop sends the transcript through the same session.send call as typed text (apps/cli/src/voice.rs). No task creation or Tasks step was found in voice.rs, so the durable background task part is not confirmed by code.

items.needs: a microphone
items.note: The voice send path is the same as typed input (apps/cli/src/voice.rs, session.send). No voice-specific document output or open control was found. Searched apps/cli/src/voice.rs, apps/cli/src/documents.rs and all of apps/cli/src for docx and pdf references; the document result depends on what the agent produces, which this code audit did not confirm.

items.where: /save-skill typed after a task finishes (optionally followed by a name)
steps: Finish a normal task in agi.
Type /save-skill and press Enter, optionally with a name after it.
Wait for the agent to write the skill file and show it to you.
Check that the file exists at .agiworkforce/skills/<name>/SKILL.md in the project folder, then start a new task that needs it and see whether the skill is used. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Save the task you just finished as a reusable skill

items.note: The command sends a prompt that asks the agent to write .agiworkforce/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs, save_skill_prompt). Whether the skill then appears in the Skills list was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: /save-routine typed after a task finishes (optionally followed by how often it runs)
steps: Finish a normal task in agi.
Type /save-routine and press Enter, adding how often it should run, or leave it blank and answer the agent's question.
Wait for the agent to create the routine with cron_check tool and state the schedule and what each run does.
Wait for the first scheduled run and check that it did the same work and finished successfully. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account

labels.text: Turn the task you just finished into a scheduled routine

items.note: /save-routine only sends a prompt that makes the agent call cron_create (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs, save_routine_prompt). It does not run the cloud admit check that /schedule uses. The step 3 tool name is cron_create, not cron_check: correct it when following this. Whether the scheduled run succeeds is not shown in code.

items.needs: a Desktop app and a CLI session in the same folder
items.note: CLI sessions are stored with the source value cli in apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs (source_to_stored). The desktop app's local-sessions list and folder filter are not in apps/cli, and the cited lib.rs line moved. The CLI side starts with agi resume (apps/cli/src/lib.rs, Continue previous session). The desktop screen words were not found in apps/cli.

items.where: agi code handoff typed in the repository folder
steps: Push any unpushed commits: the handoff refuses while commits are not pushed.
In the repository folder, type agi code handoff and press Enter, optionally with a local session id.
Read the review shown and answer the prompt to continue, or use -y to skip the prompt.
Open the cloud session link printed at the end and check that the history and pending work came with it. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a git repository with a pushed branch, a local session in that folder

labels.text: Continue a local session in a new cloud Code session

items.note: The cited lib.rs:2774 moved. The handoff command is the Handoff variant of CodeSubcommand (apps/cli/src/lib.rs). handle_code_handoff refuses with an unpushed-commit message (apps/cli/src/lib.rs) because the cloud session clones the pushed branch.

items.where: agi projects link <project> typed in the shell, then agi started in the same folder
steps: Sign in to the account and make sure the privacy mode is Managed (project knowledge is used only in Managed mode).
In the folder, type agi projects link followed by the project name or id.
Start agi in that folder and ask a question that the project's instructions or files should answer.
Compare the answer with the project's instructions and sources. If a notice says the turn runs without your project's knowledge files, the link did not take effect.
items.needs: a signed-in account with an account project

labels.text: Link this directory to an account project by id or name.

items.note: The CLI has no in-chat picker for a notebook or project. The link is made in the shell, and the word notebook is not used in apps/cli. Grounding is in apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs (project_conversation).

items.where: agi, any chat message sent after the usage limit is reached; read the error text
steps: Use the account until its usage limit is reached (a test account at its limit is easiest).
In agi, send any message.
Read the error: it gives a reset time, and if a model is listed it says Your plan also includes that model. It can also show a billing or plans link.
Type /model with the named model, send the message again, and check that the chat continues. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a Free account or a paid account at its usage limit

labels.text: Run `agi usage` to see when it resets.
Add credits or fix billing at

items.note: The named alternative appears only when a cached model list has a model other than the limited one (apps/cli/src/errors.rs, plan_alternative). The purchase link appears only for the billing recovery path. The one-step switch uses the /model text shown in the error.
